findings.title: writeConfig can now throw in PUT /api/settings and the call is not caught
findings.recommendation: Reject CR/LF/NUL in these fields during validation, or wrap writeConfig and return 400. Add a test.
findings.evidence: default_model (line 122, after setSetting) and openai_tts_key (line 349, after the voice writes) call writeConfig without a try/catch. A value with an embedded CR/LF/NUL gives an unhandled 500 and a partial SQLite write. Injection is still prevented and no secret leaks. Same family as the known pre-existing write-before-validate behavior.

findings.title: writeConfig key format is not strictly constrained
findings.evidence: A key starting with '#' or with surrounding whitespace is dropped or normalised by readConfig. All current callers use constant keys, so this is not exploitable today.

findings.title: No same-origin/content-type guard on the local key-write POST (pre-existing pattern)
findings.recommendation: In a later task, add an app-wide Origin/Sec-Fetch-Site or Content-Type: application/json check on mutating routes.
findings.evidence: request.json() accepts a text/plain cross-site simple POST, so a malicious page could replace the Gemini key with an attacker's key. /api/config has the same issue; this predates the change.

findings.title: Untracked local launch config present
findings.recommendation: Keep it out of the commit (gitignore or leave untracked).
findings.evidence: Known and out of scope: a local dev file that must not be committed.
